subject: Request: Uptime guarantee & latency commitments for Orchid Analytics
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@orchidanalytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:12:00Z
Subject: Uptime / latency guarantees for upcoming rollout

Hi Sean,

We're prepping for a large customer rollout at Orchid next quarter and procurement just pushed for explicit commitments on both uptime and P95 latency for the parts of our stack that will hit Redwood. Their ask is to see a written uptime guarantee (they quoted 99.99%) and an upper bound on p95 tail latency for 1–4k token responses.

A few constraints from our side:
- We need a signed appendix by 5/20 to make our quarter-end commitments.
- We're open to carving out scheduled maintenance windows but they want daytime reliability for US customers.
- Pricing sensitivity: if guarantees require reserved capacity / dedicated pools we'd need a clear delta.

I've attached Orchid_SLO_Request.pdf which has the procurement language. Can we discuss feasibility and an estimate for cost uplift?

Thanks,
Samir
Director of Engineering
Orchid Analytics

Attachment: orchid_slo_request.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-03T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Uptime / latency guarantees for upcoming rollout

Hi Samir — thanks for the details and the PDF. Looping in Product (Marissa), Infra (Karthik) and Legal/Commercial (Laura) to scope this.

High level: we can usually support stronger availability for strategic customers but it typically requires a combination of dedicated capacity, stricter routing/fallback rules, and an agreed canary/validation window. I want to surface a couple of internal questions so we can come back with a clean ask for procurement:
1) Is Orchid willing to commit to reserved/dedicated pool or do you need guarantees on shared fleet?
2) Are there preferred maintenance blackout windows?
3) Expected qps / tokens per minute during peak?

Marissa — attaching Orchid's request. Can you and Karthik sketch options (e.g., 99.9% on shared, 99.95/99.99 on dedicated with maintenance carveouts) plus a ballpark cost multiplier? If Legal needs an SLA appendix template I can flag that with Laura.

Next: propose a 30–60 minute sync early next week after we have options. Samir — what time zone is best?

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T09:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Uptime / latency guarantees for upcoming rollout

Thanks Sean — I reviewed the Orchid SLO request and sketched three pragmatic offerings (attached uptime-options.xlsx):

Option A — Standard (no change):
- Shared fleet, best-effort routing
- Target availability: 99.5% (no SLA credits)
- No changes to price

Option B — Commercial Guarantee (recommended compromise):
- Dedicated pool with soft isolation (reserved slots on multi-tenant infra)
- Target availability: 99.95% (scheduled maintenance carveout: 4 hours/month)
- P95 latency target: <800ms for 1–2k tokens on committed pool (subject to workload variability)
- Monthly service credit ladder for missed SLOs (limited to 10% invoice cap)
- Approx. 1.6x price uplift (estimate)

Option C — High-commitment (highest engineering cost):
- Fully dedicated nodes, strict routing, increased cache reservation
- Target availability: 99.99% (maintenance carveouts allowed outside business hours)
- P95 latency target: <500ms for 1–2k tokens
- Tighter credit/penalty terms, independent validation period
- Approx. 2.4x price uplift + engineering onboarding fee

Questions for internal owners:
- Karthik / Dev: rough eng effort + timeline to provision dedicated pool + telemetry changes?
- Laura: commercial/legal constraints, maximum credit exposure we can accept for an early-stage account?

I've attached the spreadsheet with cost delta estimates and a suggested SLA appendix skeleton. If we want to move forward with B or C, we'll need an infra estimate and a 30-day canary plan.

Attachment: uptime-options.xlsx

---
Note: Samir — if Orchid can confirm which option they prefer (B is usually a good commercial tradeoff) we'll prioritize a deep-dive with Infra/CS next week.

-Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-04T11:10:00Z
Subject: RE: Uptime / latency guarantees for upcoming rollout

Quick technical read: the options look reasonable but call out a few caveats for the team and for the customer so expectations align.

- Dedicated pool provisioning: lead time ~2–3 weeks for reserved nodes + config tuning; if we need physical isolation (on-prem or private deployment) add 4–6 weeks.
- KV cache: to hit P95 <500ms for 1–2k tokens we need increased KV reservation; that reduces effective capacity per GPU by ~20–30%.
- Routing/fallback: to guarantee daytime reliability we should implement automatic regional failover + latency-based routing; that means cross-region replication for KV snapshotting (additional infra cost).
- Monitoring/validation: require a 30-day canary to validate observed SLOs, with agreed test traffic and black-box probes.

Estimated eng effort: 2.5 FTE-weeks (provisioning + observability tweaks + runbook updates) to be ready for a B-level commitment; C-level needs an extra 4–6 FTE-weeks and a small infra spend estimate.

I'll spin up a short PRD + runbook template if we decide to proceed. For now, Marissa: does the 1.6x uplift assume we can amortize the KV reservation across other reserved customers? If not, the uplift could be higher.

-Karthik
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-05T08:37:00Z
Subject: RE: Uptime / latency guarantees for upcoming rollout

Agreed course of action based on the options we've seen: proceed with a timeboxed pilot under Option B constraints with the following must-haves before commercial sign-off:

1) 30-day canary window with agreed test harness and success criteria (pass/fail thresholds for availability and latency).
2) SLA appendix that limits credit exposure to a capped percentage of the committed fees (recommend 10%) and excludes force majeure and scheduled maintenance carveouts.
3) Operational runbook and escalation path; Vivek, please draft an incident response appendix covering on-call rotation and RCA timelines.
4) Legal to prepare a narrow, account-specific SLA appendix; do not expose precedent language for other customers.

Marissa / Sean: please prepare a one-page exec summary (option chosen, uplift, canary dates, estimated infra spend) for commercial review. Once we have exec sign-off we can present the appendix to Orchid and lock dates.

-Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@orchidanalytics.com>, Nadia Lopez <nadia.lopez@orchidanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-06T10:15:00Z
Subject: RE: Uptime / latency guarantees for upcoming rollout

Samir / Nadia — thanks for the patience while we scoped internally. Short summary and proposed next steps: 

What we can commit to now:
- Pilot approach: 30-day canary in a dedicated soft-reserved pool (Option B) starting as soon as Orchid confirms by 5/10.
- Commercial guarantee after successful canary: 99.95% uptime with a scheduled maintenance carveout (4 hours/month) and P95 latency target <800ms for 1–2k token responses on the committed pool.
- Financials: estimated uplift ~1.6x (detailed numbers in the attached spreadsheet). Credit exposure capped at 10% of the committed monthly invoice.

Operational asks from Orchid:
1) Provide a representative test traffic profile and preferred blackout windows for maintenance.
2) Procurement to confirm willingness to commit to the reserved pool and sign the SLA appendix after legal review.

Next steps
- We will circulate an SLA appendix draft and a one-page exec summary by EOD 5/06 (attached).
- Proposed call to review appendix & timelines: 5/7 at 11am PT — let me know if that works.

If Orchid agrees to the pilot terms, we can aim to complete the canary by mid-June and flip to commercial terms thereafter. Please confirm which option you want to proceed with (B recommended).

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla-appendix-draft.pdf
